paragraphs: My name is Sam, and I'm nine. I live in an old house with my parents. My grandparents live with us too. I'm their grandson. I'm the son of Mom and Dad. Our house has five things to do. Grandma writes them on a big paper. The paper is on the kitchen wall. We all read it every day. Our house is near a small park and a big tree.

Number one: Put your shoes next to the door. Number two: Walk on every stair. Number three: Wash your hands before dinner. Number four: Take a shower in the evening. My parents take theirs after dinner. I sing in the shower, and Mom laughs. Number five: Be quiet after nine o'clock. Grandpa goes to bed at eight o'clock. He is tired after a long day.

Do I like these five things? Yes, I do. They are easy, and they help everyone in the house. But Grandpa never walks on the stair. He runs, and Grandma shouts, "Slow down!" I laugh, and Grandpa laughs too. My parents say, "Grandpa is a child again." Our house is old and small. But it is a very happy house.
